# Gaṅgā: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Gaṅgā** is what the evidence put back.

Gaṅgā's myths are hydrology as theology: the river's own biography — source, fall, and ford — told as the goddess's descent to save the dead. King Sāgara's sixty thousand sons were burned to ash by the sage Kapila's glance; only Gaṅgā's water could free their souls.  Generation after generation prayed, until Bhagīratha won the boon: the heavenly river would descend.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Gaṅgā
- **ASCII form:** ganga
- **Meaning:** "The river Ganges personified — eldest daughter of Himavat, brought from heaven by Bhagīratha's austerities"
- **Domain of influence:** Sacred River, Purification
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** गङ्गा
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 85 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Gaṅgā** to *ganga* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Macron: long a: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Gaṅgā** lives at [/sites/ganga/](/sites/ganga/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ganga/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ganga/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ganga/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Gaṅgā** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Environmental & Climate Services** — Namami Gange is India's largest river-restoration program; the purifier is now the sector's flagship client.
- **Freshwater & Hydrology** — The Ganges herself, the holiest water in the world to a billion people — a river supply that is also a goddess.
- **Disaster Resilience & Recovery** — The purifier; the river that restores.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Sanskrit tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Rig Veda](/texts/rig-veda/) and [Ramayana](/texts/ramayana/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/ganga/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Gaṇeśa** ([read it here](/sites/ganesha/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Gaurī** ([read it here](/sites/gauri/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
